title: Standard error of the sample mean
problem: Random samples of size $n = 100$ are taken from a population with $\mu = 60$ and $\sigma = 15$. Find the standard error of $\bar{X}$ and describe the distribution of $\bar{X}$.

steps.instruction: Since $n = 100$ is large, apply the Central Limit Theorem to describe the distribution of $\bar{X}$.

answer: The standard error is $1.5$, and $\bar{X}$ is approximately normally distributed with mean 60 and standard deviation 1.5.

title: Normal approximation to the binomial
problem: $X \sim B(100, 0.4)$. Using the normal approximation, find $P(X < 35)$.

steps.instruction: Check the normal approximation is valid ($np \geq 5$ and $n(1-p) \geq 5$), then find the mean and standard deviation.
steps.working: $np = 40 \geq 5$ and $n(1-p) = 60 \geq 5$, so the approximation is valid. Mean: $\mu = np = 100 \times 0.4 = 40$. Standard deviation: $\sigma = \sqrt{np(1-p)} = \sqrt{100 \times 0.4 \times 0.6} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$

steps.instruction: Use the standard normal table to find the probability.

title: Using the empirical rule
problem: $X \sim B(400, 0.5)$ is approximated by $N(200, 100)$ (SD = 10). Use the empirical rule to find $P(180 \leq X \leq 220)$.

steps.instruction: Express the interval in terms of standard deviations from the mean.
Apply the empirical (68–95–99.7) rule: approximately 95% of values lie within two standard deviations of the mean.

answer: $P(180 \leq X \leq 220) \approx 0.95$. (Empirical rule: within 1 SD ≈ 68%, within 2 SD ≈ 95%, within 3 SD ≈ 99.7%.)
